phase.name: Setup and data models
phase.goal: The repository, environment, Kaggle data and data model classes are ready.

steps.step: The private repository already exists (github.com/nguyenphuquang1234567/study-manager). Add Ronald Han as a collaborator.
Create the project layout: app.py, models.py, data_processing.py, analysis.py, visualization.py, tests/, data/, README.md.
Add a .gitignore containing .venv/, __pycache__/, .pytest_cache/, data/study_log.csv and data/grades.csv (the user's own files are created by the app, not committed).
Create a virtual environment. Write requirements.txt with streamlit, pandas, numpy, scipy, matplotlib, pytest, and install them.
Write pytest.ini containing "[pytest]" and "pythonpath = ." so the tests can import the modules.

Download dataset_study.csv from Kaggle (andreylss/study-hours-vs-grades-dataset, MIT license) into data/. Check: columns student_id, study_hours, grade; 5000 rows; no missing values. Write down the real min and max of study_hours (the data card says 0-12, the histogram shows 0-10).
In models.py, write the exception classes: StudyManagerError (base), InvalidEntryError, DataFileError, InsufficientDataError.

In models.py, write the StudySession dataclass (date, course, hours, note). validate() raises InvalidEntryError for an empty course, hours of 0 or less or above 24, or a future date. to_dict() returns one row for study_log.csv.

In models.py, write the GradeRecord dataclass (date, course, assessment_type, assessment_name, score). validate() raises InvalidEntryError for empty text, a type other than quiz or exam, a score outside 0-100, or a future date. to_dict() returns one row for grades.csv.

doneWhen.check: pip install -r requirements.txt works in a new virtual environment.
StudySession with hours -1 raises InvalidEntryError; GradeRecord with score 100 is accepted.

phase.name: Data processing with Pandas
phase.goal: User data can be loaded, cleaned, saved and summarized.

steps.step: In data_processing.py, write load_csv(path, required_columns). A missing file is created with headers and returns an empty DataFrame. Pandas EmptyDataError or ParserError becomes DataFileError. A missing required column raises DataFileError.
In load_csv, convert dates with pd.to_datetime(errors="coerce") and numbers with pd.to_numeric(errors="coerce"), drop the rows that failed, and return how many were dropped.
Write save_csv(df, path), saving without the index.

Write the StudyTracker class. It loads data/study_log.csv (date, course, hours, note) and data/grades.csv (date, course, assessment_type, assessment_name, score), keeps a skipped_rows count, and has add_session() and add_grade(), which take a validated dataclass, append it with pd.concat and save.

Add StudyTracker.courses() (sorted set of course names), hours_by_course() (groupby course: total hours, session count, average session length), weekly_hours() (pd.Grouper with freq "W") and summary_stats() (totals, averages, and the hours-vs-score correlation when there are 3 or more points).

Add StudyTracker.hours_per_assessment(): pd.merge_asof(sessions, grades, on="date", by="course", direction="forward") assigns each study session to the next assessment of the same course; then groupby and sum to get total hours per assessment. This matches the meaning of study_hours in the Kaggle data.
Add StudyTracker.hours_since_last_assessment(course): the hours not yet assigned to any assessment.

Create data/sample_study_log.csv (about 30 sessions across 2 courses) and data/sample_grades.csv (about 10 assessments: at least 5 in one course and 2-3 in the other). Add load_sample_data(), which copies them over the user files.
Check one assessment by hand: add up its sessions on paper and compare with hours_per_assessment().

doneWhen.check: From a Python shell, the sample data loads and hours_per_assessment() returns the expected table.

phase.name: Prediction with SciPy, then handoff
phase.goal: Predictions work in every case, and Ronald can build on the code without waiting for answers.

steps.step: In analysis.py, write the PredictionResult dataclass: predicted_score, model_used (course, personal or baseline), slope, intercept, r_squared, p_value, n_points, warnings. explanation() returns a plain sentence such as "Each extra hour is associated with +4.8 points (r squared 0.62, p = 0.01, 8 assessments)."

Write GradePredictor.fit(hours, scores), which wraps scipy.stats.linregress. Raise InsufficientDataError when there are fewer than 5 points, and when all hours are identical (linregress raises ValueError in that case).
Write GradePredictor.from_csv(path): load the Kaggle file with load_csv, fit the baseline, and store hours_range (min, max).

Write predict(hours, course=None, personal_data=None). Negative hours raise InvalidEntryError. Use the course's own model if that course has 5 or more assessments; otherwise all of the user's assessments if there are 5 or more; otherwise the Kaggle baseline. Clip the score with np.clip(score, 0, 100). Add a warning when the hours are outside hours_range or the score was clipped.
Write regression_line(model, n=100) using np.linspace, for drawing fitted lines.

Check in a shell: the baseline slope is near 5 and the intercept near 40; predict(5) is about 65; predict(30) returns 100 with a warning; with the sample data, the course with 5 assessments uses "course" and the other course falls back.
Add docstrings and type hints to every public class and function in models.py, data_processing.py and analysis.py.
Handoff: push everything, then tell Ronald which functions each tab should call (StudyTracker methods, GradePredictor.predict, the PredictionResult fields) and how to load the sample data.

Write your individual reflection now while it is fresh (150-250 words): what you built, one technical challenge (for example matching sessions to assessments with merge_asof), how you solved it, and what you learned.

doneWhen.check: In one shell session, the sample data produces a PredictionResult from each of the three models.
Ronald confirms he can import and call everything.

phase.name: Streamlit interface and charts
phase.goal: The complete user flow works in the browser.

steps.step: In app.py: st.set_page_config, title, sidebar, and four st.tabs (Log Study, Log Grade, Statistics, Prediction). Create the StudyTracker, and load the GradePredictor in a function cached with st.cache_resource. app.py only calls into the modules; it does no calculations itself.

Log Study tab: st.form with a date (no later than today), a course (pick an existing one or type a new one), hours (0.25 to 24, step 0.25) and an optional note. On submit, build a StudySession inside try/except InvalidEntryError: show st.warning on error, otherwise save, show st.success and reload the data. Below the form, a table of sessions filterable by course.
Log Grade tab: the same pattern with GradeRecord (date, course, quiz or exam, name, score), plus a table of grades.
Sidebar: a "Load sample data" button that only works after ticking a confirmation checkbox, since it replaces the current data. Show the number of skipped malformed rows when it is not zero.

In visualization.py, write plot_prediction (faded Kaggle points, baseline line, the user's own points highlighted, the personal line when there is one, and the predicted point) and plot_hours_by_course (bar chart). Each returns a Matplotlib Figure with a title, axis labels and a legend, and shows a message instead of an empty chart when there is no data.
Statistics tab: four st.metric cards (total hours, number of sessions, average session length, average score), the per-course table and the hours-by-course chart.

Prediction tab: a course selector; hours pre-filled with hours_since_last_assessment(course); the predicted score (st.metric); the model used; a table of slope, intercept, r squared, p-value and number of points; the explanation sentence; one st.warning per warning; the prediction chart.
If time allows: plot_weekly_hours and plot_grade_history in the Statistics tab.

doneWhen.check: streamlit run app.py starts without errors.
After loading the sample data and logging one session and one grade, the Statistics tab updates.
The Prediction tab shows "course" for the course with 5 assessments and a fallback model for the other course.

phase.name: Tests and error handling
phase.goal: The logic is covered by automated tests and the app never crashes on predictable problems.

steps.step: tests/test_models.py: negative hours raises InvalidEntryError; score 105 raises InvalidEntryError; scores 0 and 100 are accepted.

tests/test_data_processing.py, using tmp_path for every file: a CSV missing a required column raises DataFileError; missing files start empty and are created with headers; hours_by_course gives the right totals for a small known DataFrame; hours_per_assessment counts sessions between two exams only toward the second; malformed rows are dropped and counted.

tests/test_analysis.py: fit on exact data y = 40 + 5x returns slope 5 and intercept 40; very high hours are clipped to 100 with a warning; identical hours raise InsufficientDataError; predict falls back from course to personal to baseline as data is removed.
Run pytest and fix until all 12 tests pass.

Trigger each problem in the running app; it must show a message, not a traceback: bad input in both forms; data/grades.csv deleted, filled with random text, or missing its score column; a row with hours "abc"; dataset_study.csv renamed (logging must still work and only the Prediction tab is disabled, with download instructions); a course with 1 assessment, or with identical hours; 30 hours entered for a prediction.
Pin the installed versions of the six libraries in requirements.txt (from pip freeze). No new features after today.

doneWhen.check: Every problem in step 5 was triggered and the app showed a message.

phase.name: README and submission
phase.goal: The project is documented, runs from a fresh clone, and is submitted before the end of the day.

steps.step: README.md sections: Project Description (with one screenshot); Features; Data (the three CSV files and their columns, the Kaggle URL, the MIT license, and a note that the Kaggle data is synthetic, generated as grade = 40 + 5 x hours + random noise); Installation (python -m venv .venv, activate it, pip install -r requirements.txt); How to Run (streamlit run app.py, then Load sample data); How to Test (pytest); Project Structure; How the Prediction Works; Known Limitations.

README section titled "Team Contributions": Quang Nguyen - setup, data models and validation, data processing with Pandas, SciPy prediction (P1-P3). Ronald Han - Streamlit interface, visualizations, tests and error handling, documentation (P4-P6).
Fresh-clone test: clone the repository into a new folder, create a new virtual environment, follow only the README, and run the app and pytest. Fix anything that breaks.
Write your individual reflection (150-250 words): what you built, one technical challenge, how you solved it, and what you learned.
Final check that the submission contains: all source code, README.md, requirements.txt, the data files, passing tests, a working Streamlit app, the Team Contributions section, and both reflections.
Submit in the format the instructor asks for (zip or repository link) and confirm it went through.

doneWhen.check: Submission confirmed before the end of 2026-12-01.
